data.title: PDCD4 inhibits translation initiation by binding to eIF4A using both its MA3 domains
data.authors: Suzuki C; Garces RG; Edmonds KA; Hiller S; Hyberts SG; Marintchev A; Wagner G
data.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Structural and biophysical work on human proteins
data.finding: Both MA3 domains of PDCD4 bind the N-terminal domain of eIF4A and compete with eIF4G and RNA for it, which explains how PDCD4 blocks translation initiation.
